transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together to discuss the lot of 1,200 cast aluminum housings currently on hold due to cosmetic residue from the forming operation. Before I can make any decision on authorizing rework and releasing a campaign plan, we need to go through our standard pre-authorization review. I'd like to hear from process engineering, maintenance, quality, and EHS on whether we can use the ultrasonic cleaning cell for this rework, and what inspection and documentation we'll need before release. Let's start with process engineering -- can you walk us through what caused the residue and whether ultrasonic cleaning is the right approach?

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from a process trial I completed yesterday. The trial showed that the residue can be successfully removed from only 900 of the 1,200 housings using the ultrasonic cleaning cell. The remaining 300 housings have embedded residue that cannot be removed by this method, and they will have to remain on hold. I have not yet entered this result into the production release system, but I wanted to make sure everyone here is aware before we proceed with the pre-authorization review.

During my weekly walkdown of the ultrasonic cleaning cell, I found that the circulation-pump seal needs to be replaced before we can use the cell for any rework. That's a planned 4-hour downtime. I haven't opened the maintenance work order yet, but we'll need to factor that into the campaign timeline.

I confirmed in the customer control plan this morning that every reworked housing must receive dimensional scanning, and the plan requires exactly 30 reworked housings to be retained for customer review. I received the revised plan from the customer portal this morning, but I have not yet updated our local inspection instruction to reflect these requirements. We'll need to factor dimensional scanning capacity and the retention of 30 units into our campaign plan before we proceed.

transcript.text: I need to share an important finding from my waste review. The spent cleaning solution from this rework campaign must be collected in exactly 2 sealed waste totes and shipped under a waste manifest. I confirmed the classification with our site's waste contractor this week, but I have not yet updated the area waste-board notice to reflect this requirement. We'll need to ensure the 2 totes are staged and the manifest is prepared before the campaign begins.
